turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_constrained_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_constrained_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Both of these hard constraints apply to every candidate:
  1. molybdenum content at most 3.21 wt%;
  2. alloying cost index Σ (price_e × wt%_e) at most 450, using the prices in USD/kg: C 0.5, Mn 2, Si 2.2, Cr 9, Ni 17, Mo 25, V 30, Nb 45, Co 33, Al 2.4, Ti 12, Cu 9.
A candidate that violates either constraint is worth zero, so picking one wastes a slot. Using the training data, predict which FEASIBLE candidates have the HIGHEST yield strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Step 1: Apply the hard constraints to the pool

**Mo ≤ 3.21 wt% violations:** c030 (3.58), c049 (3.73), c055 (3.22), c058 (3.67), c059 (4.55) → excluded.

**Cost index ≤ 450 violations** (cost dominated by Co×33, Ni×17, Cr×9, Mo×25, Nb×45): several otherwise attractive high-Co/high-Ni recipes fail, e.g.
- c015 ≈ 469, c037 ≈ 494, c065 ≈ 480, c086 ≈ 530+, c099 ≈ 576, c020, c025, c032, c045, c057 (≈ 458), c072, c089, c098, c005, c006 (≈ 475), c008, c040, c027, c077, c085 → all excluded.

## Step 2: What drives yield strength in the training data

Looking at all training rows above ~1950 MPa (2080, 2073, 2065, 2051, 2041, 2027, 2018, 2016, 2009, 2007, 2005, 2395…), a clear recipe pattern emerges:
- **Co ≈ 4–7 wt%** is the strongest positive driver (+ roughly 30–40 MPa/wt%);
- **Ni ≈ 4–10 wt%** helps (rows with Ni > 14 are consistently weak: 1256, 1337, 1464);
- **Cr ≈ 5–10 wt%**, **Mo ≈ 1–3 wt%** present in most top rows;
- **quench_temper** (and to a lesser degree quenched/solution_aged) dominates the top of the list; annealed rows cap lower;
- aging temp ~500–740 °C and non-trivial aging time appear in most top rows; solutionizing temp and cooling rate are weakly informative.

## Step 3: Score the feasible candidates against this profile

| cand | HT/route | Co | Ni | Cr | Mo | cost | comment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c044 | QT/cast | 4.72 | 6.49 | 6.69 | 0.95 | 387 ✓ | near-clone of 2073/2005 MPa training rows, aging 660 °C, 28 h |
| c029 | quenched/wrought | 4.86 | 9.04 | 6.25 | 0.66 | 421 ✓ | matches 1925–2041 MPa rows (Co+Ni sweet spot, aging 661 °C) |
| c092 | QT/AM | 6.75 | 1.80 | 6.88 | 2.60 | 435 ✓ | high-Co + high-Mo, like 2007 MPa (Co 6.3/Mo 3.1) and 1967 MPa rows |
| c082 | SA/wrought | 4.45 | 8.20 | 6.62 | 0.89 | 388 ✓ | matches 1976 MPa SA-wrought row (Co 3.8/Ni 10, aging ~700 °C) |
| c019 | SA/AM | 6.09 | 1.59 | 4.58 | 2.66 | 385 ✓ | matches 1952 MPa SA row (Co 5/Mo 1.6, aging 705 °C, long time) |

Runners-up (good but slightly weaker profile): c064 (annealed penalty), c069 (Ni 12, low Co), c075 (Ni = 0), c003 (Mo = 0, very short aging), c095/c073 (annealed).

## Selection

The five feasible candidates best matching the high-strength Co-rich, Ni-moderate, quench-temper/aged profile:

**Final: c044, c029, c092, c082, c019**
